body:
The retention state-machine proptest (crates/platform/chio-store-sqlite/src/receipt_store/tests/retention.rs, state_machine::prop_retention_preserves_append_invariant) wedges the Build-lint-test and MSRV lanes on GitHub runners: it enters, prints "has been running for over 60 seconds", and never completes (2.5h+ before the job timeout kills it; previously it ate the 6h default ceiling). Locally it finishes in ~34s at the same case count.

Evidence:
- MSRV job 91320792529 (run 30682002563, 2026-08-01): entered 05:10:04, never finished; orphan chio_store_sqlite test binary killed at 07:38.
- Identical wedge on main runs 30318286801 / 30677720699 predecessors, and on PRs #1017/#1030/#1042 (last printed test before every 6h cancel is this binary).
- Reducing per-op health folds to rotation boundaries and halving cases (48 -> 24, PR #1044) shrank local runtime to 34s but did NOT cure the runner wedge, so this is a liveness problem, not throughput.

Hypothesis: the test uniquely combines enable_background_checkpoints (background signer thread) with archive_receipts_before rotation racing appends over a synchronous=FULL file-backed store; under runner-grade fsync latency an interaction livelocks. head_property, with the same store profile but no background checkpointer/rotation, completes ~24 cases in ~8.5 min on the same runner.

The test is quarantined with #[ignore] in the hot lanes (PR #1044). Reproducing the livelock (e.g. under strace/dtruss with artificial fsync latency, or a loom model of the checkpointer/rotation handshake) and restoring the lane is the follow-up here.
title: prop_retention_preserves_append_invariant wedges CI runners (livelock under slow fsync)
